newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 9.

text.p: Instant fines for cannabis considered: Justice Minister Doug Graham said on Tuesday that cannabis users might be better dealt with by instant fines than convictions, despite opposition from his Coalition colleagues. Earlier this week, Associate Treasurer Tuariki Delamere called for decriminalisation of cannabis. Page 1.

Working party to look at curbing dangerous dogs: A Parliamentary working party was being set up to look at ways of "phasing out" dangerous dog breeds, Local Government Minister Christine Fletcher said on Tuesday night. Page 1.

Peters manipulating super referendum, says Nat MP: Debate within the Coalition over the compulsory-superannuation referendum is turning into a scrap, with National MP Brian Neeson accusing Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Tuesday of manipulating the referendum for his own ends. Page 1.

NZ First may not back National's legislation: The NZ First caucus will not necessarily give its backing to a backlog of legislation proposed by the previous government according to whip Ron Mark. Page 2.

Women's advocacy post put on hold: The establishment of a women's commissioner by the government will be delayed as it considers other options for the role. Women's Affairs Minister Christine Fletcher said she doubted the $1 million a year set aside for the position would be adequate and as an interim measure she was considering establishing an advocacy group from women's groups and non-government organisations. Page 2.

PM Won't take action on Banks: Prime Minister Jim Bolger did not intend to take action against National MP John Banks for revealing confidential Cabinet information, a spokesman for Bolger said on Tuesday. Banks, in advance publicity for his biography, revealed that the Queen had been "hurt and disappointed" by New Zealand's move towards republicanism. Page 2.

Kirton pledges food safety: Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton said on Tuesday that he would make sure consumer protection was included in a joint New Zealand-Australia policy on genetically engineered foods. Page 2.

Wilson still in race for council parking: Wilson Parking has made a revised application to the Commerce Commission for clearance to buy the Wellington City Council parking buildings, suggesting the multinational is still in the chase for the four central-city sites. Page 12.

Unhappy recovery predicted: Economic growth is expected to be about three percent a year during the next three years, with government spending the dynamo in the coming two years, according to a National Bank forecast. Page 12.

Manufacturers achieve higher export sales: Manufactured exports returned to growth in the December quarter after 15 months of weakening, making up for slower domestic sales, according to WespacTrust's analysis of manufacturing industries. Page 12.

Max Resources told off after leaking forecasts: Max Resources was censured by the Stock Exchange for providing to Auckland sharebrokers information that should have been disclosed to the market. Page 13.

Defiance fends off Bunge: Defiance Mills is urging its shareholders to reject the Bunge Foods Queensland takeover offer on the basis of a higher valuation of the sahres by Price Waterhouse Corporate Finance in Australia. Page 13.

Dairy facts boosted: The Dairy Board plans to step up the world-wide promotion of the nutritional benefits of its products in a bid for greater edge in the international marketplace for consumer dairy products. Page 13.
